key_insight: This perspective paper argues that making biological data truly "AI-ready" requires answering four foundational questions, rather than simply collecting more data or applying larger models. The core message is that data quality, context, standards, and usability must be defined explicitly for AI to work reliably in biology.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the ambiguity around what "AI-ready" means for biological data and why many datasets still underperform in machine learning workflows. It seeks to clarify the requirements biological data must meet so AI models can learn from them effectively and produce trustworthy results.
method: Frames the discussion around four guiding questions for defining AI-ready biological data.
Synthesizes challenges across data generation, annotation, interoperability, and downstream model use.
Provides a conceptual model for evaluating whether biological datasets are suitable for AI/ML applications.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper offers a practical lens for assessing whether biological datasets are fit for training, validation, and deployment. It helps reduce model failure caused by poorly curated or poorly defined data and supports more reproducible, interpretable biomedical AI.
visual_elements: A central "AI-ready data" checklist with four surrounding question bubbles
A pipeline diagram showing biological data flowing from collection to AI model training
An icon-based comparison of raw data vs curated AI-ready data
A layered framework illustration for quality, metadata, standards, and usability
paper_title: Four questions for AI-ready biological data
